downloads.heading: Download PrivacyNotes

downloads.apkFootnote: Needs Android 7.0 or newer. Zapstore, Obtainium and the APK need no Google account and no Google billing: Pro unlocks via web checkout. The APK alerts you in-app when a new version is ready.
downloads.linuxRequirement: Both formats need webkit2gtk 4.1: Ubuntu 22.04 or newer, Debian 12 or newer, or an equivalent release from 2023 onward. Older distributions only ship webkit2gtk 4.0 and cannot run these builds.
downloads.linuxArchX86Desc: Nearly every desktop and laptop. Pick this if unsure.
downloads.linuxArchArmDesc: Raspberry Pi, ARM laptops, Linux in a VM on an Apple Silicon Mac
downloads.debFootnote: Updating an existing <highlight>.deb install</highlight>? Do not uninstall it first. Double-clicking the file dead-ends in Ubuntu's App Center, which only reports that the app is installed, so install the new one over the old one from a terminal. Use the line that matches your machine; dpkg --print-architecture prints which one you need:
downloads.availability: Available now: macOS 13+, Windows 10+, iOS 15+, Linux and Android.
downloads.betaNote: All our apps are in beta and may still have bugs, so the web version is the most stable for now. Every app auto-updates and we ship fixes almost daily.

mood.heading: Track what you actually feel.
mood.intro: Mood, emotions, sleep, medication and activity level, all in a few taps. Everything is encrypted on your device before it syncs.
mood.cardEmotionsBody: 24 research-backed emotion tags. Name what you feel, spot patterns over time, and export data your therapist or doctor can work with.
mood.cardSleepBody: Five-level quality scale plus optional hours. Activity from sedentary to intense. The analytics correlate these with your mood automatically.
mood.cardMedsBody: Configure once, tap daily. Tracks taken vs. skipped, dosage changes over time, and correlates adherence with mood. Supplements, birth control, ADHD meds, antidepressants. See what's working and share the data with any provider on your terms.
mood.cardAnalyticsBody: Client-side analytics detect correlations between sleep, activity, medication, and mood. Export a printable PDF report for your doctor or copy a structured prompt for AI analysis.
mood.encryptedBody: Nobody logs their antidepressant dosage in Notion. Nobody tracks hopeless days in a Google Doc. Data this sensitive needs zero-knowledge encryption, so that is how PrivacyNotes is built.

whyPrivacy.heading: Most note apps read your notes.<accent>Ours can’t.</accent>
whyPrivacy.para1: Most note apps mine your content. Add “buy a new TV” to your shopping list and your next few pages fill up with TV ads. Your grocery list, your journal, your private thoughts, all fed into ad-targeting pipelines, profiled, and sold. That is the business model of every “free” note app backed by advertising.
whyPrivacy.para2: Even apps that don’t show ads still store your notes in plaintext on their servers, readable by employees, hackable in breaches, and available to anyone with a subpoena. Your data becomes their leverage.
whyPrivacy.differenceBody: <brand/> is end-to-end encrypted with keys that never leave your device, so neither we nor our servers can read what you write. There is no tracking, no analytics, no advertising and no profiling, and there never will be. What you write stays yours.
whyPrivacy.keyboardNote: A note on device keyboards. Third-party keyboards (such as Gboard, SwiftKey, or Samsung Keyboard) may send what you type to their own servers. This happens at the operating-system level, outside any app’s control. Consider disabling cloud features in your keyboard settings or using an offline-only keyboard.

readIt.heading: Do not trust us. Read it.
readIt.body: The app you are running is published, along with the encryption inside it and the database it talks to. Start with the one-minute check that needs no tools, or go straight to the code.

wontFind.kicker: What you won’t find in the app

noRecovery.heading: Your phrase is your key
noRecovery.body: No phrase, no notes. We cannot recover them, and neither can anyone else. That is the trade-off for end-to-end encryption: under self-custody you are the only one holding the key, so writing to our team cannot bring your notes back.
noRecovery.noRecoveryDesc: Lose your phrase, lose your notes
noRecovery.deviceDesc: With self-custody, your phrase never touches our servers
noRecovery.zkDesc: With self-custody, we can't read or restore your data
noRecovery.printDesc: View and export your phrase any time
noRecovery.googleDesc: You still get a phrase. Back it up

about.intro: <brand/> is a zero-knowledge workspace for your notes, tasks, files and vault. Your 12-word phrase derives a key in your browser; every byte on the server is encrypted; under self-custody, nobody (including us) can read your notes. Data stored in <nowrap>Switzerland</nowrap>. Encrypted on your device, and it works offline, too.

about.tagline: No subscriptions. Just Software. Not a service.
about.hotkeysFootnote: Most shortcuts are ignored while you're typing in a text field, so regular keys like J and K still type J and K.

trust.openSourceBody: The app and the encryption inside it are published, so anyone can check our zero-knowledge claims.
trust.dataStorageBody: Encrypted blobs stored in Zurich, 🇨🇭 Switzerland.
trust.faviconsBody1: Website icons (favicons) come from DuckDuckGo and Google, fetched by our server on your behalf. Your browser never contacts either one, so they see our server asking for a domain and never see you.
trust.faviconsBody2: Icons are cached on your device for 90 days. No request includes your identity, and you can turn icons off in Settings > Appearance.
